etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Old French apte, from Latin aptus, from obsolete apere (“to fasten, to join, to fit”), akin to apisci (“to reach, attain”); compare with Greek ἅπτειν (háptein, “to fasten”) and Sanskrit आप्त (āpta, “fit”), from आप् (āp, “to reach, attain”).

definitions.definition: Suitable; appropriate; fit or fitted; suited.

quote.citation: 1678, Antiquitates Christianæ: Or, the History of the Life and Death of the Holy Jesus: […], London:  […]  E. Flesher, and R. Norton, for R[ichard] Royston, […], →OCLC:
quote.text: a river  […]  apt to be forded by a lamb

quote.citation: 1755, Callimachus, “The First Hymn of Callimachus. To Jupiter.”, in William Dodd, transl., The Hymns of Callimachus, […], London:  […]  The translator [William Dodd], […], →OCLC, page 1:
quote.text: While we to Jove the pure libations pay, / Than Jove what apter claims the hallow'd lay?

definitions.definition: (of persons or things) Having a habitual tendency; habitually liable or likely; disposed towards.

quote.citation: 1874, John Lubbock, Scientific Lectures / On Plants and Insects:
quote.text: This tree, if unprotected, is apt to be stripped of its leaves by a leaf-cutting ant.

quote.citation: 1886, Frederic Harrison, The Choice of Books:
quote.text: that lofty pity with which prosperous folk are apt to remember their grandfathers

quote.citation: 1961 November 10, Joseph Heller, “The Soldier in White”, in Catch-22 […], New York, N.Y.: Simon and Schuster, →OCLC, page 168:
quote.text: Since sick people were apt to be present, he could not always depend on a lively young crowd in the same ward with him, and the entertainment was not always good.

definitions.definition: Ready; especially fitted or qualified (to do something); quick to learn.

quote.citation: 1599 (first performance), William Shakespeare, “The Tragedie of Iulius Cæsar”, in Mr. William Shakespeares Comedies, Histories, & Tragedies […] (First Folio), London:  […]  Isaac Iaggard, and Ed[ward] Blount, published 1623, →OCLC, [Act III, scene i]:
quote.text: Fulfill your pleasure. Live a thousand years, / I shall not find myself so apt to die.

quote.citation: 2010, David Dondero, Just a Baby in Your Momma's Eyes:
quote.text: Where our apt used to be they built a fancy condominium high-rise.Which at a lowly income none of us could ever really quite afford.
